engine.description:
Which simulation fits the module just taught, or "none". Choose one ONLY if it can pose a task about this material; a simulation about something adjacent is worse than cards, because it costs the student minutes. Options: 
- microscope = Compound Microscope (biology) — can pose: bring the slide into sharp focus at one named total magnification, starting from a stated state the instrument was left in; or work up the objectives in order, bringing the specimen into focus at every power on the way rather than only at the top one. Scores the sequence, not the endpoint
- molecule-builder = Molecule Builder (chemistry) — can pose: build one specific named molecule from individual atoms; or build any molecule that satisfies one structural constraint, where more than one answer is correct
- none = nothing here fits, so write cards instead.

sentence.description: One sentence telling the student what to do in the simulation, addressed to them. Alexandria says this, never the simulation, so it must stand alone. Leave it empty when engine is "none".

card_type.description: What kind of card this whole set is; every card in it is this kind. multiple-choice asks the student to commit to one of several answers. flashcard asks them to recall the answer themselves and then rate how well they did. Choose flashcard when the material is worth generating from memory, multiple-choice when the interesting part is the wrong turns a student takes.

front.description: The question, for multiple-choice; the cue to recall from, for a flashcard. It must be answerable from the module the student just read.

options.description: multiple-choice only. Exactly one option is correct. Every wrong option must be a mistake a real student actually makes here, never a filler answer.

text.description: The option as the student reads it.

response.description: What the student is told the moment they pick THIS option. For a wrong option, name the specific misunderstanding that leads to it. For the correct one, say briefly why it is right. Never say "correct" or "incorrect" alone.

answer.description: multiple-choice only. The index of the correct option in `options`.

back.description: flashcard only. The answer the student is checking themselves against.

cards.description: A set of cards on the module just taught. It plays while the next module is being written, so it has to be worth real seconds without being homework.

power.description: The TOTAL magnification to finish at. The eyepiece is fixed at 10x and the objectives are 4x, 10x and 40x, so these three totals are the only ones the instrument can reach — there is no oil-immersion objective and 1000x is not available.

specimen.description: What is on the slide, and the only two things this engine can draw. onion-epidermis is a field of brick-shaped plant cells with nuclei; newsprint-letter-e is the classic lowercase e cut from newspaper, which shows that the image arrives inverted and reversed. Never name a specimen outside this list — the engine will report an error rather than draw the wrong thing.

start.description: The state the instrument is found in. as-found-on-low-power is the tidy case. as-found-on-high-power leaves the 40x objective swung in with the stage far below focus, which forces the student to go back down to low power because coarse focus is locked at 40x. stage-racked-to-the-top starts the stage at the end of its upward travel so the student has to cross the focal plane coming down.

slide_label.description: The words written on the slide's paper label, drawn on the glass in the side view. It is a property of the object on the stage, e.g. 'Onion epidermis' or 'Newsprint e'. It is NOT an instruction and NOT the task sentence — the chrome says the task, and the engine never restates it.

task_microscope__focus-specimen.description: Parameters for microscope, task kind "focus-specimen". Ask the student to bring the slide into sharp focus at one named total magnification, starting from a stated state the instrument was left in. Fill this in ONLY if you chose engine "microscope" and this kind.

top_power.description: The total magnification to finish at. 100x requires focus at 40x then 100x; 400x requires focus at 40x, then 100x, then 400x, in that order. 40x is not offered as a top power because a one-rung ladder is not a series.

specimen.description: What is on the slide, and the only two things this engine can draw — onion-epidermis or newsprint-letter-e. Never name anything else.

slide_label.description: The words written on the slide's paper label, drawn on the glass in the side view. A property of the object, never an instruction and never the task sentence.

task_microscope__power-series.description: Parameters for microscope, task kind "power-series". Ask the student to work up the objectives in order, bringing the specimen into focus at every power on the way rather than only at the top one. Scores the sequence, not the endpoint. Fill this in ONLY if you chose engine "microscope" and this kind.

formula.description: The molecular formula to build, written plainly, e.g. H2O, CH4, NH3, C2H6, CH4O. Only H, C, N and O are available, and the builder models SINGLE BONDS ONLY — never ask for a molecule that needs a double or triple bond, so no O2, no CO2, no N2, no CH2O.

name.description: The common name of that molecule, e.g. water, methane, ammonia, ethane, methanol.

task_molecule-builder__build-target.description: Parameters for molecule-builder, task kind "build-target". Ask the student to build one specific named molecule from individual atoms. Fill this in ONLY if you chose engine "molecule-builder" and this kind.

constraint.description: The structural property the student's molecule must have. Every atom must still end up with a full valence, and the builder models single bonds only.

task_molecule-builder__free-build.description: Parameters for molecule-builder, task kind "free-build". Ask the student to build any molecule that satisfies one structural constraint, where more than one answer is correct. Fill this in ONLY if you chose engine "molecule-builder" and this kind.
